about: The gospel of the Second Sunday of Advent. John the Baptist, already in prison, sends to ask whether this is He. The answer is not a claim but a list of what can be seen, and it ends with a word about John himself.

s01.translation: At that time, when John heard in prison of the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples and asked Him:

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s02.translation: Are You the One who is to come, or should we look for another?

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s03.translation: Jesus answered them: Go and report to John what you have heard and seen.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s04.translation: The blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, and the Gospel is preached to the poor; blessed is the one who does not stumble because of Me.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s05.translation: As they went away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: What did you go out into the desert to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s06.translation: What then did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft garments?

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s07.translation: Behold, those who wear soft garments live in royal houses.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s08.translation: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s09.translation: For this is the one of whom it is written: Behold, I send My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way before You.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

w049.gloss: have the gospel preached to them

w061.explanation: Latin “abeúntibus illis” expresses a whole clause: “when they were going away”.
